interpretation: The 2026 paper-derived competition term improves the held median error by 17.53 percent versus per-channel constants and the no-competition Poisson control, so it contains a real density-shape effect.

It is nevertheless 78.30 percent worse than the already retained characteristic-slope baseline and has only 0.15 median per-channel rank correlation. The compact marginal does not explain the first-party Kodak 250D granularity curve shape.
The Stanford report and derivative profiles remain an informative external algorithm baseline, not an independent material measurement or stock calibration source.
forbidden_rescue: Do not change uniformity, density normalization, floors, shared amplitude, split, controls or gates on this cohort.
next_ready_leaf: Advance a new measured observation or a mechanism-distinct developed-image experiment; do not add Poisson-binomial capacity or spatial decoration to rescue this failed marginal.
claim_ceiling: Negative held-exposure evidence for one 2026 paper-derived Poisson-binomial density marginal against first-party Kodak 250D typical granularity curves.
